# Admin Console Abuse Case Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: falcon-20261011-0416-full-f5cb7c9
- Repository: falcon (`MaineCyberTech/falcon`)
- Branch: main
- Commit SHA: `f5cb7c96cacefb2e8b1dedc1f15e633d9072264b`

- Area code: ADMIN
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/falcon-20261011-0416-full-f5cb7c9/26_admin_console_abuse_case_audit.md`
- Scope limitations: the "admin console" surface is the operator UIs (Grafana, OpenSearch Dashboards, ntopng, ntfy, Wazuh dashboard, DFIR-IRIS, UniFi) plus host/root tooling. Vendor UI internals were not audited beyond declared/live configuration; Cloudflare Access state was read read-only via the zone API.

## Scope

Reviewed: admin pages/APIs, user/org/role management, billing panels (N/A), document/ticket admin (IRIS), webhook/API key admin, bulk ops, approval flows, impersonation, settings, exports, destructive actions, confirmations, permissions, rate limits, undo/recovery, tests.

Not reviewed: vendor UI code paths (Grafana/OSD/IRIS internals), the edge-sensor repo, Cloudflare account-level configuration beyond the zone read.

## Executive Summary

The operator consoles are the crown jewels of this stack; their exposure model is unchanged: Cloudflare Access at the edge for falcon/iris/soc, per-service application logins at the origin, basic auth for ntopng, native auth for ntfy (now internal-only), and a default-deny host firewall. This run verified one improvement and three persisting issues:

1. **ADMIN-P2-001 (still open)** — consoles have no origin authentication. Live origin probes reproduce login-page redirects; the API read shows the falcon Access app now enforces for the owner IP (bypass removed) while iris/soc still bypass the owner NAT. The `/ntop` route remains the only origin-authenticated console.
2. **ADMIN-P2-002 (still open)** — the Access-posture gate still accepts origin reachability: `external-smoke` runs on the lab runner and treats any 302 as OK; the latest run (2026-10-10) logged iris/soc via the "owner-IP Access bypass; origin reachable" branch. The enroll check accepts 404, which masked the dead enrollment hostname until the 2026-10-11 verification.
3. **ADMIN-P2-003 (still open)** — no centralized actor-level audit for Grafana/ntfy/IRIS admin actions: container logs are `json-file` local, the Wazuh agent has no container-log source, the Traefik access log carries no user identity (always `"-"`) and is unrotated (72 MB), while OpenSearch REST audit and the Wazuh indexer audit are live and healthy.

Strengths: no self-privilege escalation path (single admin per console, no user-management UI exposed to a lower role, no impersonation, no bulk destructive console operations), destructive host tooling is root-gated with dry-run/ledger, OpenSearch/Wazuh auth events are audited, and the container estate has no privileged containers or docker.sock mounts.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Console exposure and origin authentication

- Evidence: `dynamic.yml:87-132`; live probes; Access API; `ACCESS_AND_ACCOUNTS.md` §5-§6; `risk_register.md` R-15.
- What it does: publishes Grafana/OSD/ntop/IRIS/Wazuh consoles via Cloudflare Tunnel + Access.
- Current controls: Access (falcon/iris/soc), app logins, ntopng basic auth, host firewall allowlist, rate limits.
- Missing controls: origin auth on Grafana/OSD/IRIS/Wazuh; Access-JWT validation.
- Risks: edge-only enforcement; the owner-NAT bypass is active for iris/soc (API-verified), so anything behind that NAT reaches those consoles without an Access challenge.
- Recommended improvement: origin auth or Access-JWT validation; otherwise record acceptance against R-15 with the current policy set (the R-15 mitigation text still cites "ntfy basic auth", which no longer exists as a public control).

### Item: Access-posture verification (`external-smoke`)

- Evidence: `.github/workflows/external-smoke.yml:20-26` (comment says "Must run from GitHub's network" while `runs-on: [self-hosted, lab]`), `:33-46` (any 302 passes; non-Access 302 labeled "owner-IP Access bypass; origin reachable"), `:60-68` (summary still claims "must be 302 to cloudflareaccess.com"); run 38067043888 log.
- What it does: daily public-surface availability + Access-posture check.
- Current controls: reachability check works; the Access-posture assertion is gone.
- Missing controls: a vantage that can distinguish Access-enforced from origin-reachable; no service-token/API check.
- Risks: an Access app removal/misconfiguration for iris/soc would not be detected; the workflow stays green (latest run 2026-10-10 green).
- Recommended improvement: restore an external vantage (or a scoped Cloudflare API check) and fail on non-`cloudflareaccess.com` redirects; stop accepting 404 for enroll (it masked a dead hostname); split availability (lab) vs posture (external/API).

### Item: Admin action auditability

- Evidence: `config/docker/daemon.json` (`json-file` 20 MB × 5); live Wazuh agent localfiles (no container-log source); `bootstrap/60-host-auditd.sh` (host file watches); `bootstrap/60-central-deploy.sh:216-227` (OpenSearch REST audit, live `security-auditlog-2026.10.11` 3,863 docs); live Traefik access log (`ClientUsername` always `"-"`, 72 MB, no rotation); live Grafana single admin; ntfy ACLs.
- What it does: records host identity/config changes and OpenSearch/Wazuh auth events.
- Current controls: auditd, OpenSearch security audit, Wazuh audit, decision log, rotated container logs.
- Missing controls: actor-level audit for Grafana/ntfy/IRIS console actions (logins, role/settings changes, deletes, exports) shipped to a durable/central store; Traefik access-log rotation.
- Risks: an abusive admin action on those consoles leaves only rotated local logs; no alerting on admin-action anomalies.
- Recommended improvement: ship container logs into the Wazuh/OpenSearch pipeline (Wazuh docker-listener or a Vector source), enable Grafana audit where available (Enterprise-only), and add rules for admin role/settings/delete events; add logrotate/maxSize for the Traefik access log.

## Findings

### Finding ID: ADMIN-P2-001 - Admin/observability consoles are exposed through public routers without origin authentication

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High (config + live probes + Access API)
- Area: ADMIN
- Evidence:
  - `config/traefik/dynamic.yml:87-132` (grafana, dash, iris-public, soc-wazuh routers carry only `sec-headers`/`public-rate-limit`; only `falcon-ntop` has `falcon-basic-auth`)
  - Live origin probes 2026-10-11T04:26Z: `/`→302 Grafana login, `/dash/`→302 OSD login, `/ntop`→401, iris→302 `/dashboard`, soc→302 `/app/login`
  - Cloudflare zone API: falcon app has no owner-IP bypass (challenge enforced); soc/iris apps carry `bypass-owner-public-ip` 142.105.190.25/32 — anything behind that NAT reaches those consoles without an Access challenge (live-verified)
  - `docs/runbooks/ACCESS_AND_ACCOUNTS.md` §5-§6; `ledgers/risk_register.md` R-15 (OPEN; mitigation text stale)
- What is happening: The consoles are reachable through the tunnel with only application logins at the origin; the sole network gate is Cloudflare Access at the edge plus the host firewall.
- Why it matters: An Access policy error/removal or a shared-NAT actor reduces protection to the application login; there is no origin-side control to fail closed.
- User / business impact: Admin console exposure beyond the intended Access gate.
- Security / privacy / reliability impact: Edge-only enforcement of the SOC/monitoring consoles.
- Recommended fix: Put an origin auth layer (or Access-JWT validation) in front of the console routers; alternatively record the residual acceptance explicitly against R-15 with the current live evidence and update the stale mitigation text.
- Suggested validation: staging Access-app removal test asserting origin denial; repeat live probes for all public hostnames and attach to the risk acceptance.
- Owner suggestion: @owner
- Effort estimate: M
- Dependencies: Cloudflare config for Access/JWT or service tokens
- Status: still-open (prior ID ADMIN-P2-001; same root cause as SEC-P2-001)
- Endpoint / data path: public hostname → cloudflared → Traefik → console container
- Attack path: Access bypass/misconfig → app login brute force → console admin abuse

### Finding ID: ADMIN-P2-002 - The Access-posture gate accepts origin reachability; no automated check verifies Cloudflare Access enforcement anymore

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High (workflow + live run log)
- Area: ADMIN
- Evidence:
  - `.github/workflows/external-smoke.yml:20-26` — comment: "Must run from GitHub's network … On the lab the vantage is internal and the result is wrong, so it stays on hosted"; `runs-on: [self-hosted, lab]`
  - `.github/workflows/external-smoke.yml:33-46` — any 302 passes; non-`cloudflareaccess.com` locations are reported "OK … owner-IP Access bypass; origin reachable"; `:47-54` accepts 404 for enroll
  - `.github/workflows/external-smoke.yml:60-68` — job summary still says "iris/soc: must be 302 to cloudflareaccess.com (Access still enforcing)"
  - GitHub Actions run 38067043888 (2026-10-10T16:17Z, success on `lab-runner-2`): log lines `OK https://iris.mainecybertech.us/ -> 302 (owner-IP Access bypass; origin reachable)` and the same for soc
  - The enroll 404 acceptance masked the dead `enroll.mainecybertech.us` ingress until the 2026-10-11 verification (INFRA-P1-003)
- What is happening: The only automated check that asserted the Access gate was relaxed to accept origin reachability from the lab vantage; the workflow self-description still claims posture verification.
- Why it matters: If the iris/soc Access apps are removed or misconfigured, CI remains green; the compensating control for the exposed consoles is no longer machine-verified.
- User / business impact: Silent loss of the edge control that gates the SOC consoles.
- Security / privacy / reliability impact: Verification gap on the primary control for admin-console exposure.
- Recommended fix: restore a trustworthy posture check (external vantage or scoped Cloudflare API/service-token check); fail on non-Access redirects; stop accepting 404 for enroll (or assert the expected token-gated status); rename/split the workflow if the lab vantage is kept for availability only.
- Suggested validation: mutate a staging Access policy and assert the check fails; or simulate a non-Access 302 and assert failure.
- Owner suggestion: @owner
- Effort estimate: S
- Dependencies: external runner or scoped Cloudflare API token
- Status: still-open (prior ID ADMIN-P2-002; also tracked as TEST-P2-001)
- Endpoint / data path: CI → https://iris.mainecybertech.us/, https://soc.mainecybertech.us/
- Attack path: none directly; this removes detection of an Access regression

### Finding ID: ADMIN-P2-003 - No centralized actor-level audit trail for Grafana/ntfy/IRIS console admin actions

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High (log config + live agent config + live access-log sample)
- Area: ADMIN
- Evidence:
  - `config/docker/daemon.json` — container logs use `json-file` with 20 MB × 5 rotation (local only)
  - Live host Wazuh agent localfiles (2026-10-11T04:25Z): journald, `/var/log/audit/audit.log`, `active-responses.log`, `dpkg.log` + `df`/`netstat`/`last` commands — **no Docker container-log source**
  - `bootstrap/60-host-auditd.sh` — watches identity/sudoers/ssh/firewall/secret metadata only
  - `bootstrap/60-central-deploy.sh:216-227` — OpenSearch REST audit enabled (live: `security-auditlog-2026.10.11` 3,863 docs); Wazuh indexer audit `internal_opensearch` (live)
  - Live Traefik access log: JSON fields include `ClientUsername`, but all sampled values are `"-"` (no authenticated user); the file is 72,102,901 bytes with no logrotate entry and no Traefik maxSize
  - Live Grafana: single `admin` account; live ntfy ACLs (monadmin admin); IRIS app login
- What is happening: Admin activity in Grafana, ntfy and IRIS is recorded only in rotated container-local logs; there is no durable, centrally searchable audit of who did what (logins, settings/role changes, deletes, exports) for those consoles. OpenSearch and Wazuh auth events are audited.
- Why it matters: The prompt's abuse cases (self-escalation, role/delete/export actions) cannot be reconstructed for the non-OpenSearch consoles; a compromised or careless admin leaves little durable evidence.
- User / business impact: Weaker incident reconstruction and accountability for the consoles that control monitoring/alerting and case data.
- Security / privacy / reliability impact: Audit/observability gap.
- Recommended fix: Ship container logs into the Wazuh/OpenSearch pipeline (Wazuh docker-listener, or a Vector source reading the json-file logs), enable app audit features where available, add detection rules for admin role/settings/delete/export events, and add logrotate/maxSize for the Traefik access log.
- Suggested validation: perform a read-only admin action in a maintenance window and verify an event lands in OpenSearch.
- Owner suggestion: @owner
- Effort estimate: M
- Dependencies: log-shipping decision + Wazuh/Vector config
- Status: still-open (prior ID ADMIN-P2-003)
- Endpoint / data path: console container stdout → json-file → (not shipped) → no central audit
- Attack path: admin console abuse leaves only local rotated logs
